title: Fulcher's illness and death in 1977
summary: Fulcher kept hiring musicians from his sickbed despite strokes, told the crowd to listen, and died in 1977; Leeman feels his presence still.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Late sixties, Jim Fulcher's mouth deteriorated, but all the while, though ill, he was foremost in setting the Odessa jazz parties up each year, calling us all personally from his sick bed to hire us, and he wouldn't have it any other way. He wanted to do it personally, and a series of strokes took their toll.

And he came to the sessions with a cane, and he wouldn't miss them for the world; his strength was taxed most of the time, but he'd sit there smiling and make his one announcement each year, telling the people to shut up and listen to the music, that they were making too much damn noise. There were quite a few people that made those parties not solely for the jazz, but to socialize and make it a society event.

The ladies and the gentlemen there would sport their latest creations from Dallas and Fort Worth -- it was party time for them. So Fulcher would tell them to shut up and listen to the music. But still to go on -- he progressively got worse until a massive stroke, and his death two years ago in 1977. End of that part of the story.

But we still go on, and I'll be there this May, and many other musicians he loved will be there, too. I believe that Jim Fulcher will be with us, also. It's a wierd feeling that we can't see him, but we will feel him.
